## Frequently asked questions

**What causes stress eating?**

Stress eating happens when we use food to cope with difficult emotions like anxiety, loneliness, or overwhelm. It's a learned behavior, not a character flaw. At BCC, we help clients understand their relationship with food and build healthier coping skills through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**How do I stop compulsive stress eating?**

Stopping compulsive eating starts with understanding the emotions and situations that trigger it. Our program teaches practical coping skills, mindful eating practices, and personalized strategies to interrupt the cycle. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional support, and cooking classes in one program, helping clients develop sustainable tools to manage stress without turning to food.

**What are ADHD eating habits?**

People with ADHD may experience impulsive eating, forgetting meals, binge eating, or difficulty recognizing hunger and fullness cues. At BCC, we work with clients who struggle with these patterns through behavioral therapy and dietary guidance. A licensed therapist or your medical provider is the right person to discuss ADHD diagnosis and treatment options.

If emotional or stress eating is affecting your life, we're here to help. Reach out to learn how our program can support you.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy and counseling. At BCC, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors work with clients on coping skills, goal setting, mindful eating, and family engagement. We provide group and individual therapy as part of our comprehensive behavioral healthcare program for obesity, addressing emotional eating, binge eating, and chronic overeating in a supportive, structured environment.

**What's involved with bariatric surgery?**

Bariatric surgery is a medical procedure your surgeon can explain in detail. At BCC, we provide behavioral support that can complement surgery or stand alone as treatment for obesity. Our program includes behavioral therapy and counseling, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. We coordinate care with referring medical providers and help clients develop sustainable coping skills and healthy eating patterns.

**Why can't you eat rice after bariatric surgery?**

Your bariatric surgeon and medical team are the right people to answer specific dietary questions after surgery. At BCC, our registered dietitians provide nutrition education and meal planning to help you navigate eating guidelines, whether you've had surgery, are taking weight loss medications, or are pursuing behavioral treatment for obesity. We also offer grocery store tours and guidance on navigating dining out to support long-term success.

**How long does it take to lose 50 pounds with gastric bypass?**

Weight loss timelines vary by individual, and your surgeon can give you medical guidance on what to expect. At BCC, we focus on the behavioral side of obesity treatment. Our Intensive Outpatient Program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions, helping clients build sustainable coping skills, understand their relationship with food, and develop healthy eating and movement habits. We do not promise weight loss outcomes, but we do provide comprehensive behavioral support.

If you're looking for behavioral support before or after bariatric surgery, or as standalone treatment for obesity, reach out to learn more about our program.

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps people understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy and counseling. **What kind of therapy helps with weight loss?**

Behavioral therapy that addresses the psychological and emotional aspects of eating is most effective. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education in one intensive outpatient program. Our approach helps clients develop sustainable coping skills and a healthier relationship with food, whether as standalone treatment or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medications.

**Why is it mentally hard to lose weight?**

Weight struggles often involve emotional eating, stress, trauma, or long-standing patterns with food that go far beyond willpower. That is why we focus exclusively on the behavioral treatment of obesity. Our team helps clients work through the underlying issues, build coping skills, and create lasting change through counseling, nutrition education, and hands-on support in our teaching kitchen and movement classes.

**How does bariatric surgery affect mental health?**

Bariatric surgery can bring emotional challenges alongside physical changes. Our program supports people before or after surgery by addressing the behavioral and psychological aspects of weight management. We help clients navigate the mental health side of their experience through counseling, coping strategies, and ongoing support. For questions about surgery itself, your bariatric surgeon is the best resource.

If you are looking for behavioral support for obesity or eating struggles, we would be glad to talk with you about whether our program is a good fit.

payload.title: Tue 11/24: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI:
Patients on weight loss medications often see dramatic physical results, but lasting change requires the behavioral half: the habits, coping skills, and relationship with food that keep the result after treatment.

The Bariatric Counseling Center provides group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. Call it two business days.

We accept most health insurances. Uniquely, the program is in-network with most health insurance plans, and patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide discharge summaries. We accept most health insurances. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

payload.title: Thu 11/26: Lunch at the desk, again
payload.purpose: The workday eating pattern, without shame, and what dietary guidance in the program does with it.

captions.LI:
You're eating lunch at your desk again.

Not because you planned to. Not because it's the healthier choice. Because that's what the workday asked of you today.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance starts exactly there. Not with a meal plan that pretends your calendar is empty. With the calendar you actually have.

Our registered dietitians work with the rhythm of your real day. The meetings that run long. The commute. The desk lunch. We build nutritional strategies that fit the life you're living, not the one a textbook imagines.

That's part of what makes this program different. Dietary guidance that meets you where you are. Behavioral therapy that helps you understand your relationship with food. Cooking classes that make planning easier. Mindful movement that fits your schedule. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, the Bariatric Counseling Center offers an Intensive Outpatient Program designed for people who struggle with weight loss, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We're in network with most health insurance plans.

Learn more at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/program-schedule.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas
payload.alt_text: A desk lunch scene with the text 'Dietary guidance for your real day' overlaid.
payload.why_now: Posted on Thanksgiving week when many working professionals face disrupted eating schedules and feel guilt about desk meals during a holiday-shortened workweek.

Referring a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center takes two business days from submission to scheduled intake.

Providers can submit referrals by email to intake@bccsanantonio.com, by fax to 210-764-1129, or by calling our Director of Admissions, Leloni Gonzales, at 210-634-2200.

We ask for the patient's name, contact information, insurance details, and the referring provider's NPI number. Our team confirms insurance eligibility, contacts the patient directly, and schedules their first session.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications that patients receive from their medical providers. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide progress notes as requested.

The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients both onsite in San Antonio and virtual across Texas. We accept most health insurances, and our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits.

Refer a patient at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/refer-a-patient/.

## Frequently asked questions

**What are the 4 C's of addiction?**

The 4 C's are craving, loss of control, compulsion, and continued use despite consequences. These patterns show up in food addiction just as they do in other addictive behaviors. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful movement education.

**How can I mentally stop food cravings?**

Managing food cravings involves learning coping skills, identifying triggers, and practicing mindful eating. Our program teaches recovery and coping skills in a supportive environment with licensed therapists, registered dietitians, and a professional chef. We help clients develop sustainable strategies to respond to cravings without relying on willpower alone. Real change comes from understanding why cravings happen and having tools to address them.

**What is the most common food addiction?**

People often struggle with highly processed foods that combine sugar, fat, and salt. But food addiction is not really about one specific food. It is about the relationship someone has with eating. We focus on helping people who struggle with binge eating, compulsive overeating, and chronic over-eating, regardless of which foods are involved.

**What support groups exist for people with eating problems?**

We provide group therapy as part of our Intensive Outpatient Program, where clients meet two to three times per week for about three months. Our groups are led by licensed professional counselors and a clinical psychologist, not peer-led. This structure allows for clinical guidance alongside the peer support that makes group work so valuable.

If you are struggling with food addiction or compulsive overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a psychological evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

A psychological evaluation assesses whether you are ready for surgery and helps identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect your success. At BCC, our licensed therapist or clinical psychologist conducts a thorough assessment and provides a detailed letter to your surgeon. We also offer ongoing behavioral support through our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**Why do I need a psych eval for bariatric surgery?**

Most surgeons require a psychological evaluation to ensure you are prepared for the lifestyle changes surgery requires. The evaluation looks at your relationship with food, emotional eating patterns, coping skills, and readiness for long-term behavioral change. Your surgeon uses this information to decide if surgery is appropriate and to plan your care.

**What does a psych eval for bariatric surgery look like?**

The evaluation typically includes a clinical interview with a licensed therapist or psychologist, along with written assessments that measure eating behaviors, mood, and quality of life. We review your medical history, weight history, and goals. Afterward, we send a letter to your surgeon with our findings and recommendations for any additional behavioral support you may benefit from.

**Is there an online psychological evaluation available for bariatric surgery?**

Yes. We offer virtual psychological evaluations via telehealth for clients throughout Texas. The evaluation is conducted by video appointment with one of our licensed professionals. Whether you meet with us onsite in San Antonio or virtually, the assessment is the same thorough process, and we provide the documentation your surgeon requires.

**How do I prepare for a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation?**

Be honest and open during the interview. There is no pass or fail. We are looking to understand your relationship with food, your support system, and your readiness for change. Bring a list of any medications you take and be prepared to discuss your weight history, eating patterns, and what you hope surgery will accomplish for you.

If you would like to schedule a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation or learn more about our program, we invite you to reach out.

**What is the root cause of binge eating?**

Binge eating often stems from a combination of emotional, psychological, and environmental factors. Stress, trauma, dieting patterns, and learned coping behaviors can all play a role. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our licensed therapists and registered dietitians work with clients to understand their unique triggers and develop healthier ways to relate to food and emotions.

**What is the difference between extreme hunger and binge eating?**

Extreme hunger is a physical need for food, often after prolonged restriction or intense activity. Binge eating typically involves eating large amounts quickly, often past fullness, and may feel out of control. Our team helps clients learn to distinguish physical hunger from emotional eating and develop intuitive eating skills that honor their body's signals.

**Why can't I stop overeating?**

Overeating is rarely about willpower. It often reflects deeper emotional patterns, stress responses, or a disconnect from hunger and fullness cues. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education to help clients understand and modify their relationship with food. One program, not four.

Our program addresses the behavioral patterns behind overeating in a compassionate, structured environment.

**How can I train my brain to stop overeating?**

Changing patterns around food takes more than willpower. It involves learning new coping skills, understanding emotional triggers, and building sustainable habits. Our therapists and dietitians work with clients on mindful eating, goal setting, and practical strategies that make lasting change possible. We teach these skills in both individual sessions and group settings, so you have ongoing support as you build new patterns.

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can be connected to many things, from stress and emotional coping to learned habits and food environments. A licensed therapist or your medical provider can help identify what may be contributing in your specific situation. Our program addresses the behavioral and emotional aspects of overeating through counseling, nutrition education, and skill-building in a supportive setting designed specifically for people struggling with weight loss and food-related concerns.

**What is the root cause of binge eating?**

Binge eating often stems from a combination of emotional, behavioral, and environmental factors. There is rarely just one cause. Our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors help clients explore what drives their eating patterns and develop healthier coping skills. We work on these issues through individual therapy, group support, and practical education around food, nutrition, and mindful eating in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

If you are struggling with compulsive overeating or food addiction, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Overeaters Anonymous worth it?**

OA meetings offer peer support and community, which many people find valuable. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we complement that approach with professional clinical care: licensed therapists, registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education in one program. We work with people who attend OA, people who have tried it, and people exploring other paths.

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can be tied to stress, anxiety, depression, binge eating disorder, or learned patterns around food. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore what is driving it in your specific situation. We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance and coping skills.

**What is the easiest way to stop overeating?**

There is no single easy fix, but understanding the emotional and behavioral patterns behind overeating is a strong foundation. We teach coping skills, mindful eating, nutritional planning and goal setting in group and individual therapy. Recovery takes time, and we provide structured support over roughly three months and 30 sessions in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**What are the controversies surrounding Overeaters Anonymous?**

Some people appreciate OA's spiritual foundation and 12-step structure. Others prefer a clinical, evidence-based approach with licensed professionals. At BCC, we respect all pathways and do not replace OA. We offer comprehensive behavioral healthcare that can stand alone or work alongside peer support groups, depending on what fits your needs.

If you are looking for professional support for overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

captions.FB:
Family engagement in behavioral healthcare for obesity

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, family engagement is part of the work. Not every session, not mandatory, but available when it helps.

A spouse learning how to support without monitoring. A parent understanding the difference between care and control. Adult children finding new ways to talk about food at gatherings.

Family sessions happen when a client asks, or when a counselor suggests it might help move something forward. The people around you don't need to be experts. They just need to understand what you're working on.

We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education in a unique, all-inclusive format. One program, not four. Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Link in the first comment.
captions.IG:
family support for weight loss and behavioral health

## What is bariatric therapy?

Bariatric therapy is behavioral treatment for obesity, binge eating and chronic overeating. It typically involves working with licensed therapists and registered dietitians to understand and modify your relationship with food, develop coping skills, and build sustainable eating and movement habits. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, we provide this care through an Intensive Outpatient Program that combines group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education. Our program runs about three months, meeting two to three times per week, and is available both onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas. We are in network with most health insurance plans, with claims processed under mental health benefits.

## Bariatric Surgery Counseling in San Antonio

Bariatric surgery counseling is behavioral health support that helps people prepare for or maintain weight loss after bariatric surgery. It involves working with licensed therapists and registered dietitians to understand and modify your relationship with food, develop coping skills, practice mindful eating, and plan sustainable nutrition and movement habits. The Bariatric Counseling Center provides this support through an Intensive Outpatient Program that includes group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education. Our approach helps clients develop sustainable coping skills and a healthier relationship with food, whether as standalone treatment or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medications.

faqs.q: Why is it mentally hard to lose weight?

## Frequently asked questions

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy and counseling. At BCC, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors work with clients on coping skills, goal setting, mindful eating, and family engagement. We provide group and individual therapy as part of our comprehensive behavioral healthcare program for obesity, addressing emotional eating, binge eating, and chronic overeating in a supportive, structured environment.

**What's involved with bariatric surgery?**

Bariatric surgery is a medical procedure your surgeon can explain in detail. At BCC, we provide behavioral support that can complement surgery or stand alone as treatment for obesity. Our program includes behavioral therapy and counseling, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. We coordinate care with referring medical providers and help clients develop sustainable coping skills and healthy eating patterns.

**Why can't you eat rice after bariatric surgery?**

Your bariatric surgeon and medical team are the right people to answer specific dietary questions after surgery. At BCC, our registered dietitians provide nutrition education and meal planning to help you navigate eating guidelines, whether you've had surgery, are taking weight loss medications, or are pursuing behavioral treatment for obesity. We also offer grocery store tours and guidance on navigating dining out to support long-term success.

**How long does it take to lose 50 pounds with gastric bypass?**

Weight loss timelines vary by individual, and your surgeon can give you medical guidance on what to expect. At BCC, we focus on the behavioral side of obesity treatment. Our Intensive Outpatient Program runs about three months and roughly 30 sessions, helping clients build sustainable coping skills, understand their relationship with food, and develop healthy eating and movement habits. We do not promise weight loss outcomes, but we do provide comprehensive behavioral support.

If you're looking for behavioral support before or after bariatric surgery, or as standalone treatment for obesity, reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**What causes stress eating?**

Stress eating happens when we use food to cope with difficult emotions like anxiety, loneliness, or overwhelm. It's a learned behavior, not a character flaw. At BCC, we help clients understand their relationship with food and build healthier coping skills through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**How do I stop compulsive stress eating?**

Stopping compulsive eating starts with understanding the emotions and situations that trigger it. Our program teaches practical coping skills, mindful eating practices, and personalized strategies to interrupt the cycle. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional support, and cooking classes in one program, helping clients develop sustainable tools to manage stress without turning to food.

**What are ADHD eating habits?**

People with ADHD may experience impulsive eating, forgetting meals, binge eating, or difficulty recognizing hunger and fullness cues. At BCC, we work with clients who struggle with these patterns through behavioral therapy and dietary guidance. A licensed therapist or your medical provider is the right person to discuss ADHD diagnosis and treatment options.

If emotional or stress eating is affecting your life, we're here to help. Reach out to learn how our program can support you.

Google shows an AI Overview for this term that cites valleyhealthpartners.org, oregonnutritioncounseling.com, weightwatchers.com, onehealthmedgroup.com, nynutritiongroup.com, youtube.com and not BCC.

## What is nutrition counseling?

Nutrition counseling is one-on-one or group guidance from a registered dietitian to help you understand how food choices affect your health and weight. It typically includes meal planning, education about portion sizes and nutrient balance, and strategies for eating in different settings like restaurants or grocery stores. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, nutrition counseling is part of our Intensive Outpatient Program for obesity. Our registered dietitians provide nutritional and meal planning, lead grocery store tours, and teach you how to navigate dining out. We offer this guidance both onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas, and sessions are in network with most health insurance plans.

initial.F: The claim BCC can make and the large eating disorder chains cannot: behavioral treatment alongside weight loss medication. 'Weight loss medications' only, never the drug class abbreviation.
initial.I:
Weight loss medications quiet the hunger signal. They do not teach the skill.

Patients on these medications often describe the same thing: "food noise," drops  and for the first time there is room to work, to think, to breathe. What we do with that room determines what happens when  the coverage changes or the prescription stops.

That work is behavioral: coping skills for stress and emotion, structure around meals, cooking, movement that is enjoyable enough to keep.

We do not prescribe. Our program can be standalone behavioral care for people with obesity, or can be in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers.

If you prescribe these medications, we would like to be the behavioral half of the plan.
initial.J: Behavioral support for people taking weight loss medications, in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas. Medication can quiet hunger. It does not teach the skills for managing stress, habits, and emotions around food, and those skills are what remain when a prescription changes or stops. The Bariatric Counseling Center of San Antonio does not prescribe. Our program can be standalone behavioral care for people with obesity, or can be in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances.

payload.title: Tue 11/24: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI:
Patients on weight loss medications often see dramatic physical results, but lasting change requires the behavioral half: the habits, coping skills, and relationship with food that keep the result after treatment.

The Bariatric Counseling Center provides group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. Call it two business days.

We accept most health insurances. Uniquely, the program is in-network with most health insurance plans, and patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Thu 11/26: Lunch at the desk, again
payload.purpose: The workday eating pattern, without shame, and what dietary guidance in the program does with it.

captions.LI:
You're eating lunch at your desk again.

Not because you planned to. Not because it's the healthier choice. Because that's what the workday asked of you today.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance starts exactly there. Not with a meal plan that pretends your calendar is empty. With the calendar you actually have.

Our registered dietitians work with the rhythm of your real day. The meetings that run long. The commute. The desk lunch. We build nutritional strategies that fit the life you're living, not the one a textbook imagines.

That's part of what makes this program different. Dietary guidance that meets you where you are. Behavioral therapy that helps you understand your relationship with food. Cooking classes that make planning easier. Mindful movement that fits your schedule. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, the Bariatric Counseling Center offers an Intensive Outpatient Program designed for people who struggle with weight loss, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We're in network with most health insurance plans.

Learn more at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/program-schedule.

on_image: Dietary guidance for your real day
San Antonio and virtual across Texas
payload.alt_text: A desk lunch scene with the text 'Dietary guidance for your real day' overlaid.
payload.why_now: Posted on Thanksgiving week when many working professionals face disrupted eating schedules and feel guilt about desk meals during a holiday-shortened workweek.

Referring a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center takes two business days from submission to scheduled intake.

Providers can submit referrals by email to intake@bccsanantonio.com, by fax to 210-764-1129, or by calling our Director of Admissions, Leloni Gonzales, at 210-634-2200.

We ask for the patient's name, contact information, insurance details, and the referring provider's NPI number. Our team confirms insurance eligibility, contacts the patient directly, and schedules their first session.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications that patients receive from their medical providers. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide progress notes as requested.

The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients both onsite in San Antonio and virtual across Texas. We accept most health insurances, and our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits.

Refer a patient at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/refer-a-patient/.

#BehavioralHealth

Our head chef, Leila Bebley, teaches recipe education and instruction in our state-of-the-art teaching kitchen. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and mindful eating education in a unique, all-inclusive format. One program, not four. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BariatricCounseling #SanAntonio #MindfulRecovery

meta: META_ACCESS_TOKEN not set. To connect Facebook and Instagram:
1. developers.facebook.com: create an app (type Business), add the Facebook Login and Instagram Graph products.
2. Graph API Explorer: pick the app, choose the BCC Page as the token owner, grant pages_read_engagement, pages_read_user_content, read_insights, instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights, ads_read.

3. Exchange it for a long-lived Page token (Access Token Debugger, Extend), then paste it in seo-tools/.env as META_ACCESS_TOKEN=... and put the Page id and Instagram Business id in social.json under own.
4. Meta Ad Library also needs one-time identity confirmation at facebook.com/ID before the ads_archive endpoint answers.
youtube: YOUTUBE_API_KEY not set. To connect YouTube (own channel and competitors):
1. console.cloud.google.com: any project, APIs and Services, Enable APIs, turn on YouTube Data API v3.
2. Credentials, Create credentials, API key. Restrict it to the YouTube Data API v3 only.
3. Paste it in seo-tools/.env as YOUTUBE_API_KEY=... and put the BCC channel id (UC...) or @handle in social.json under own.youtube_channel_id.
linkedin: LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN not set. LinkedIn is the hardest one and is optional:
